div.div:
All these WSRs are cleared sequentially during a secure wipe.
During a secure wipe no instruction executes. Thus the only collision is with the MAI.

div.div:
All 3 register are cleared simultaneously by an instruction. Can collide with a MAI execution.
When secure wiping we wipe all registers simultaneously. But the wipe happens in a dedicated cycle (where only BN MAC is wiped). But the MAI could collide.
The total required bits is > UrndLen (256+192 = 448 > 389). Thus we need a permutation.
The shuffling uses the remaing bits of the permutation.

div.div:
A MAI execution finishes when a secure wipe happens. Thus URND usage can collide during a secure wipe.
A MAI execution can also collide with an instruction that reads URND or a BN MAC instruction.
To avoid these collisions, a permutation is needed.

div.div: Memory keys are used when a fatal error is detected. The keys are used before any WSR/GPR/WDR is cleared. But an ongoing MAI execution can collide.
